subject: computer-science
source_note: Topic structure follows the OCR A-Level Computer Science specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Computer Systems
units.blurb: Processors, software, data and the wider context of computing

units.name: Algorithms & Programming
units.blurb: Computational thinking, programming and standard algorithms

units.name: Programming Project (NEA)
units.blurb: Analyse, design, develop and evaluate a real solution

topics.name: Processors, I/O & Storage
topics.blurb: CPU architecture, the fetch-execute cycle, devices and storage

topics.name: Software & Software Development
topics.blurb: Systems and application software, development methodologies and languages

topics.name: Exchanging Data
topics.blurb: Compression, encryption, databases, networks and the web

topics.name: Data Types, Structures & Algorithms
topics.blurb: Number representation, data structures and Boolean algebra

topics.name: Legal, Moral, Cultural & Ethical Issues
topics.blurb: Computing law, ethics and the impact of technology on society

topics.name: Elements of Computational Thinking
topics.blurb: Abstraction, decomposition, thinking ahead and concurrently

topics.name: Problem Solving & Programming
topics.blurb: Programming constructs, OOP and writing programs to solve problems

topics.name: Algorithms & Standard Algorithms
topics.blurb: Big-O complexity, searching, sorting and path-finding algorithms

topics.name: Analysis of the Problem
topics.blurb: Identify a real problem, stakeholders and success criteria

topics.name: Design of the Solution
topics.blurb: Plan the structure, algorithms and interface of the solution

topics.name: Developing the Solution
topics.blurb: Build and iteratively test the coded solution

topics.name: Evaluation
topics.blurb: Judge the solution against the success criteria

connections.why: Software runs on, and is shaped by, the underlying processor and devices
Knowing how data is represented underpins compression, encryption and transmission
Hardware stores and processes the binary representations of data
Development methodologies frame how programs are written to solve problems
Data structures determine which algorithms can operate on the data and how efficiently
Abstraction and decomposition are the basis of designing program solutions
Thinking ahead and logically is what designing efficient algorithms requires
Programming skill is needed to implement and analyse standard algorithms
Data exchange and storage raise privacy, security and legal questions
How software is built and used has ethical and societal consequences
Decomposing a real problem is the first step of the project analysis
Programming and design knowledge shape the planned solution
The project is built using the programming skills developed in the course
Efficient standard algorithms are applied when coding the solution
Analysis sets the requirements the design must satisfy
The development stage implements the planned design
The finished solution is judged against the original success criteria
Evaluation refers back to the requirements established in analysis
